newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire expels 11 U.N. aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Zaire expels 11 U.N. aid workers.

text.p: Zaire's government, under pressure from rebel advances in the east, expelled 11 U.N. aid workers on Wednesday despite negotiations to head off the deportations, U.N. sources said.
The government, which criticised the aid workers' weekend pull-out from Zaire's third city of Kisangani, wanted them to leave before negotiations on resuming their activities, the sources added.
"Eleven U.N. workers have been expelled," one source told Reuters.
The U.N. had been negotiating to get the 11 expulsion orders and others lifted.

The government earlier ordered the expulsion of about 40 U.N. and non-governmental organisation (NGO) workers after the weekend pullout saying that it had triggered the slaughter by rebels of thousands of Hutu refugees and displaced Zaireans.
There has been no independent confirmation of any such slaughter.
The U.N. sources said some of the expelled workers would remain across the River Zaire from Kinshasa in Congo's capital Brazzaville pending the result of negotiations.
NGO representatives said that none of their staff had been individually ordered to leave, adding that they suspected the Zairean authorities wanted to put the spotlight on the United Nations.
